question: Which class of gain is the largest one visible in a measured population statistic on 2036-12-31, and which population is counted in it?
overlapCheck:
T asks the year a capability exists; G asks whether anyone is better off for it, and the two clocks have already been measured apart. The most advanced machine-originated medicine compressed target-to-candidate to 12 to 18 months, an unambiguous move on T's quantity, and its pivotal trial reads out on 30 October 2029 because the disease takes 52 weeks to declare itself in a patient's lung function. The capability step got roughly ten times faster and the arc to a prescription stayed near a decade. G is what that decade is made of.

K measures the interval between two rungs, both of which are inside the laboratory. It says nothing about a gate outside it, and the edge runs the counterintuitive way: a short K widens G's interval rather than closing it, because it compresses only the side with no institution in front of it.

A is the closest of the ten and the overlap is real and localised. A asks whether control holds and whether anyone can tell; G6 borrows the second clause and points it at benefit. The distinction is the instrument and its owner. A's instrument is evaluations and interpretability, built by laboratories, read by laboratories. G's is trials, registries, payment records and outcome series, built by regulators, funders and health systems, and 1,466 of 1,524 device authorisations to March 2026 cleared on equivalence to an existing device rather than on an outcome — a measurement failure that no alignment evaluation would catch or repair. I have priced the correlation rather than denied it: A6 into G6 is the single largest multiplier in the edge set at 1.45.

C asks what two governments settle about capability. It touches G twice and narrowly — export controls withhold inference from the countries the cheapest benefit class serves, and a verified limit implies the standing international measurement machinery that also runs universal early-warning coverage. Otherwise a settlement between two capitals is silent on whether a clinic in a third country has a payment code.

R is the governance axis nearest to G because R writes the gate G measures, and the separation is that R asks who writes the rules and what they bind while G asks what got through. The same regime produces different G worlds depending on its evidentiary standard: a device regime that has existed for decades cleared 96.2 percent of its machine authorisations on predicate equivalence, so R5 enforced can yield G2 or G6 depending on whether liability attaches to the outcome or to the equivalence. R constrains G and does not determine it.

D is the one that needed the most work, and it comes apart from G in both directions. D measures the share of client-judged paid work completed at acceptable quality — a labour-market quantity with a paying client as the judge. Three demonstrations that G is a different quantity. First, riverine flood warning is given away, has no client, appears nowhere in a freelance-project index, and is the fastest-realised benefit in the whole record. Second, 1,524 authorised devices meet 3 permanent payment codes: the work is done, almost nobody bills for it, and the outcome is unmeasured — D is silent and G is the entire question. Third, and decisively, the two move in opposite directions in the same room: after detection tools arrived at four endoscopy centres, unassisted adenoma detection fell from 28.4 to 22.4 percent, so the work got done and the patient got worse. The reverse case exists too — sixteen experienced developers were 19 percent slower with the tools while mathematical results kept landing. D up and G down, D down and G up, both observed. That is the definition of a separate axis.

S asks what physically limits capacity, which is an input. It bears on G twice: power and siting binding is G5's mechanism seen from a household bill, and diversified capacity is the condition under which inference reaches the countries holding under 0.1 percent of world data-centre capacity today. Capacity is upstream of every position here and identifies none of them.

P asks what publics do; G asks what publics get. They are the two sides of one transaction and the record shows them decoupled — 39 percent saying the technology does more harm than good in the same years a national screening programme improved its sensitivity from 73.8 to 80.5. P has one application in the entire rule library because no rule takes public response as its subject; G gives the public response something measured to be a response to.

E asks whether the money holds. Money is a hard gate on exactly one position — a 320-patient 52-week pivotal programme and the plant behind it are funded objects, and a company cut or paused five programmes including three clinical ones in May 2025 under far milder stress — and nearly irrelevant to another, since a forecast whose compute cost per run fell three to four orders of magnitude survives a capital-expenditure cut intact. E is one gate among five. G's whole content is ranking the gates.

L asks what the laboratories choose. G asks what happens outside them, and the strongest coupling is L4 into G4: a commercial cadence sells throughput, and throughput is the gain that does not leave the building.
name: Benefit realisation
desc: The largest realised gain visible in a measured population statistic on 2036-12-31, and the population counted in it. Four quantities decide it and none of them is model capability: which class of output carries the gain, which gate stands in front of that class, the years between a capability existing and a person being better off, and who sits on the receiving side. The record on 2026-08-20 sets the zero. No medicine whose discovery is attributed to a machine holds a marketing authorisation anywhere in the world; the most advanced candidate published a 71-patient safety trial in June 2025 with a lung-function signal as a secondary endpoint and no between-arm test, and enters a 320-patient pivotal trial whose primary completion is dated 30 October 2029. The United States device authorisation list held 1,524 entries at its 30 March 2026 cut, 1,164 of them radiology, 1,466 cleared on equivalence to an existing device rather than on an outcome; three permanent payment codes existed for clinical machine services in January 2026. Against that, an intergovernmental forecasting centre has run a machine-learned model as its headline product since 25 February 2025, and riverine flood warning now reaches about 460 million people across more than 150 countries. The positions are six worlds and not one quantity graded. A world where warning reaches the poorest countries inside four years while no medicine arrives for a decade, and a world where a screening programme in a rich country cuts reading workload 44 percent while the same tool has no delivery channel in a poor one, are both realised-gain worlds and they disagree about who is counted. A position here sets the benefit clock the document draws, separately from the capability clock T sets, and carries edges from all ten existing axes.

positions.name: Forecasts land first
positions.basis: An intergovernmental centre put a machine-learned model into operations on 25 February 2025 and its ensemble on 1 July 2025; medium-range error down 5 to 15 percent against the physics model, precipitation skill up about 10 percent, verified against radiosonde and surface observations rather than against its own analysis. Cyclone track error at five days 230 km against 370 km for the incumbent ensemble, roughly a day of extra lead, used operationally in an October 2025 landfall forecast. Riverine flood prediction reliable to five days in basins with no gauges where the incumbent delivered a nowcast; about 1,800 sites, 150-plus countries, roughly 460 million people, framework opened June 2026 so national services can train their own. Chest-radiograph triage for tuberculosis recommended since 2021, recommended products four to eight in June 2025, against 2.3 to 2.4 million cases never diagnosed in 2024. Compute cost per forecast down three to four orders of magnitude.
positions.desc: The gains that arrive by the horizon are carried in outputs consumed the moment they are issued, needing no purchase, permit, plant or trial. The ordering is set entirely by whether a delivery channel already exists, and it inverts the ordering the reference text expects: the area its author was least confident about lands, and the area he was most confident about does not. The poorest countries are early rather than last here, because the tool substitutes for a scarce specialist instead of adding a billable service on top of an abundant one, and because it is given away rather than sold. Medicine, materials and freight are still inside their pipelines at the horizon. The case against this position is in the same literature: a May 2026 comparison found the machine-learned models consistently worse than the physics models on record-breaking events, underestimating both intensity and frequency, with the error growing the further an event exceeds the training window — and a warning system that fails at the events justifying it does not become a measured statistic. The second weakness is that coverage is not receipt; no published estimate exists of how many of the 460 million covered received a warning and moved.
positions.domains: Weather, tropical cyclone, riverine flood, tuberculosis triage on chest radiograph, crop advisory. Clinical medicine, materials and freight do not land inside the window.
positions.lag: One to four years, set by how long a national service takes to wire an existing warning channel to a new model. The published capability of 2023 was operational at an intergovernmental centre by February 2025, and the flood framework went from paper to open source in about two years. The gate is a phone and a broadcast channel.
positions.who: Broad and unusually flat. About 460 million people already inside flood coverage, most of them in countries holding under 0.1 percent of world data-centre capacity, and about 60 percent of one continent's population currently without effective early warning is the addressable remainder. Not counted: anyone whose gain would have needed a purchase, a prescription or a procurement.

positions.name: Rich systems absorb it
positions.basis: A Swedish randomised screening trial, 105,915 women randomised April 2021 to December 2022, final primary results January 2026: sensitivity 80.5 against 73.8 percent at identical 98.5 percent specificity, reading workload down 44 percent, cancer detection up 29 percent, interval cancer 1.55 against 1.76 per thousand at p=0.41 — the widely quoted 12 percent is the point estimate of a null. A Taiwanese pragmatic trial, 15,965 patients, 90-day all-cause mortality 3.6 against 4.3 percent, hazard 0.83, mechanism stated by its authors as not yet elucidated. Then the gate: 1,524 authorisations against 3 permanent payment codes and 23 temporary ones in January 2026; 19 software billing codes in April 2025, none billed more than 3,600 times or paid more than 200,000 dollars a year. Adoption 86 percent in system-affiliated hospitals against 37 percent in independents. Median years to availability by income group across 119 medicines and 6,871 launches since 1982: 2.7, 4.5, 6.9, 8.0, a gap unchanged over forty years.
positions.desc: The gains land where a rich health system already had a specialist to substitute for and a billing route to pay for it. This is the only class with two randomised read-outs already in hand, which is why it carries the largest prior, and it is also the class whose ceiling is set by something no model improves: an organised programme with universal invitation and two radiologists reading every film is what made the Swedish result possible, and in most low-income countries population screening does not exist at all, with measured mammography screening rates of 5.6 to 13 percent. The gate here is payment and procurement, and it is open-ended rather than long — a screening tool that works has no route to a permanent code, and four software tools held add-on payment status in 2025 against one in 2023. The instructive failure is the retinopathy model that beat specialists in the laboratory and rejected 21 percent of nurse-captured images in eleven clinics because the rooms could not be darkened. Nothing was wrong with the model.
positions.domains: Population screening, risk alerting, triage, measurement and documentation inside health systems that already run organised programmes. Molecules are absent at the horizon; the benefit is carried by information products reading images and signals.
positions.lag: Four to eight years from a working model to a randomised read-out — the Swedish trial randomised its first woman in April 2021 and published its primary outcome in January 2026, four years and nine months, for a tool already certified when the trial began. Then an open-ended payment and procurement gate. Then a further five to eight years to low-income countries on the historic ladder.
positions.who: High-income health systems holding an organised programme and a billing route. Within them, large hospital systems ahead of independent, rural, government-owned and critical-access facilities by 86 percent against 37 percent, so the diffusion is itself a distributional fact and runs against need. Not counted: the countries where the programme the tool improves does not exist.

positions.name: Molecules clear late
positions.basis: 117 machine-enabled therapeutic assets across 63 companies in interventional trials by 2026; 60 through Phase 1, 8 through Phase 2, none approved anywhere. Phase 1 success 80 to 90 percent against a 50 to 65 percent historical baseline, Phase 2 about 40 percent and level with industry — the chemistry moved, the biology did not, on a denominator of a few dozen molecules. Discovery step compressed to 12 to 18 months while the arc from target to prescription stayed near a decade; the flagship pivotal trial runs 52 weeks because that is how long the disease takes to declare itself, primary completion 30 October 2029, first approval therefore 2030 or 2031. Qualification machinery is live: a pathology tool qualified in December 2025 for use by any sponsor in a defined context, an in-silico liver model accepted into a development-tool programme in June 2026. Against it, the field's own review of 7 August 2026, 22 authors, finding clinically relevant impact disappointingly limited. And the access precedent: a hepatitis C cure available since 2013 had reached 36 percent diagnosed and 20 percent treated by 2024.
positions.desc: The compressed-century claim lands, and it lands on the trial clock rather than the model clock. First approvals in 2030 to 2033, a cohort behind them drawn from the assets now in Phase 1, and by the horizon a disease-specific mortality series moves in high-income and upper-middle-income countries for one or two conditions. This is the world where the reference text was right about direction and wrong about tempo by roughly a factor of three, which is close to what its author said in July 2026 when he stated that a rate of ten years per year is not currently achievable and named infrastructure and regulatory systems as two of the three brakes. The strongest published argument against it is not about capability at all: a 0.1 change in the correlation between a preclinical model and a clinical outcome offsets a ten- to hundred-fold change in screening throughput, and machines have demonstrated the throughput far more clearly than the correlation. The mechanism to watch is qualification, because it converts one company's validated tool into infrastructure any sponsor may use without revalidating it.
positions.domains: Small molecules and biologics with machine-originated targets or machine-designed compounds, arriving first in slowly-progressive diseases with an accepted surrogate endpoint. Materials, batteries and reactors do not complete a lap inside the window — no machine-proposed inorganic material had entered commercial production as of August 2026.
positions.lag: Ten to fourteen years from target to a person holding a prescription, of which the discovery step is one to two. A pivotal read-out dated 30 October 2029 sets the earliest first approval at 2030 or 2031, and a movement in a mortality series needs a further uptake curve on top of that.
positions.who: High-income countries first, then the historic ladder — about 1.8 years more to upper-middle, 4.2 to lower-middle, 5.3 to low-income, a spacing that has not moved since 1982. Within a receiving country the realised fraction can sit at a fifth eleven years after the cure exists, which is the observed hepatitis C figure and not a pessimistic scenario.

positions.name: Throughput stays inside
positions.basis: An evolutionary search agent at one United States laboratory found a 4-by-4 complex matrix multiplication in 48 scalar multiplications against a record of 49 standing since 1969, matched the state of the art on about 75 percent of more than fifty open problems and improved it on about 20, and its scheduling heuristic has recovered about 0.7 percent of one worldwide fleet's compute continuously for over a year, equivalent to roughly 14,000 servers. An open-problems database in mathematics went to 565 solved of 1,217 by August 2026. Germline workups reported at a tenth of their former time; literature reviews that would have taken two years. Against that: 95 percent of enterprise pilots with no measurable profit-and-loss impact across 150 interviews, 350 surveys and 300 deployments; 76 of 1,978 registered interventional machine studies with posted results; two of seventeen farm-technology bundles showing meaningful efficiency gains across 570 farms over twenty years; sixteen experienced developers 19 percent slower with the tools while believing they were 20 percent faster.
positions.desc: The capability gains are enormous, real and audited, and they are captured as throughput by whoever owns the compute and the instruments. Experiments per researcher, formal proofs, chip-scheduling heuristics, internal cycle time — all of it compounds, and none of it crosses a trial, a payment code, a plant or a border. This is the position in which the reader's two sentences stop being in tension: the machines keep getting better, the factory floor keeps finding them wrong, and no population statistic moves, because the gate in front of every class that would move one is set by biology, law or payment and not by the model. The single most credible hard-dollar gain in the entire record accrues to the company that built the model. The measured consumer surplus of 172 billion dollars in March 2026 does not contradict this: mean willingness-to-accept ran 124.50 dollars a month against a median of 11.40, so the aggregate is carried by a thin top and half of users would give the thing up for the price of a sandwich.
positions.domains: Mathematics, algorithm and heuristic search, software and scientific throughput, internal research-and-development cycle time. Clinical outcome, population health, materials in production and freight all stay inside their pipelines.
positions.lag: The benefit clock has not started while the capability clock runs at full speed. Zero laps completed in the physical domains: 380,000 stable material candidates were announced in November 2023 and none had entered commercial production by August 2026, and a candidate screened from 32 million to a working cell in under nine months has produced no shipped product in the two and a half years since.
positions.who: Whoever owns the compute and the instruments — the two or three United States frontier laboratories, the Chinese frontier laboratories, and the firms buying from them. The domains that reached people outside the industry fastest did so precisely because they were given away; the domains with the largest audited gains kept them inside the firm that built the model.

positions.name: Ledger runs negative
positions.basis: Adenoma detection in standard unassisted colonoscopy fell from 28.4 percent to 22.4 across four centres comparing the same endoscopists three months before and after detection tools arrived, an absolute 6.0 points at p=0.0089 with an odds ratio of 0.69, and each point of that rate maps to about 3 percent of interval colorectal cancer risk. A meta-analysis of 21 studies and 2,885 professionals found ambient documentation cut temporal demand while imaging tools and decision support showed mixed or paradoxically increased workload, and stated net benefit on the workforce as an open empirical question. 640 Kenyan entrepreneurs given the same assistant: high performers up just over 15 percent, low performers down about 8. One United States capacity market went from 28.92 to 329.17 dollars per megawatt-day between the 2024/25 and 2026/27 years, data centres identified as the majority driver, about 9.3 billion dollars added in one auction and roughly 70 dollars a month per household projected by 2028.
positions.desc: Deployment is broad, the tools do what they claim, and the measured net on the receiving side is flat or negative. Three mechanisms, none of which a better model repairs. The tool changes the human beside it, and the change is not in the direction of the tool's own metric. The same output helps whoever can already judge which part of it to act on and harms whoever cannot, so it stratifies exactly along the resource that was already unequal. And the industry's own physical demand raises the price of an input everyone else buys, which is a measured welfare loss landing on people who received no capability at all. This position is why the axis is not a ratchet: a world can have rising capability, rising deployment and a population statistic moving the wrong way, and one of those three movements is already documented. It is held at a modest prior because the evidence is thin — the deskilling study is observational across four centres with a three-month window and no replication, the workload meta-analysis rests on two or three studies for its significant estimates, and the grid attribution is contested at anywhere from 40 to 70 percent.
positions.domains: Endoscopy and other detection work where the human retains the unassisted task; decision support and imaging where verification burden replaces the labour saved; advisory tools given to users of uneven judgement; and electricity, where the cost lands on non-users.
positions.lag: None, which is why this direction lands first. The deskilling window was three months on either side of deployment and the capacity price moved in a single auction. Every other position on this axis has a gate in front of it; this one does not.
positions.who: Costs fall on the population and on the worker standing beside the tool; gains on the operator. The people least equipped to filter the output are the ones the same output makes worse, and the households paying the capacity charge are not the ones holding the capability.

positions.name: Record cannot say
positions.basis: 1,466 of 1,524 device authorisations to 30 March 2026 cleared on equivalence to an existing device rather than on an outcome demonstration, and the authorising agency states its own list is built by string-matching decision summaries and is not comprehensive. 4 of 86 randomised trials of machine health tools worldwide between 2018 and 2023 ran in low- or middle-income countries, which is the finding that moved three funders to commit 60 million dollars in February 2026 to establish whether the tools work at all. 76 of 1,978 registered interventional machine studies have posted results and 74 name mortality anywhere in their outcomes; of published trials, 81 percent reported a positive primary and the primaries were overwhelmingly diagnostic yield rather than a patient outcome. 71 percent of United States acute-care hospitals used integrated predictive tools in 2024 while the only systematic study of clinical use, over 11 billion billing claims, called adoption nascent and concentrated in a handful of devices. The best-known point estimate of the effect on a physical science — 44 percent more materials, 39 percent more patents, 17 percent more product innovation — was disavowed by its own university in May 2025 and was still being cited by a research commissioner afterward.
positions.desc: Deployment is wide, authorisation is routine, spending is large, and there is no apparatus capable of saying whether anyone is better off. The gate here is evidence production, which nobody funds because nobody bills for it, and which the regulatory route actively substitutes away: a clearance turns on equivalence to a predicate, so the cheapest path to market is the one that generates no outcome data. This is the least assumption-laden description of the state on 2026-08-20 and stocks of this shape persist, which is the whole argument for its prior. It mirrors A's second clause deliberately and in the same register, and the mirroring is the point — a world can be full of deployed, paid-for, apparently working machines and contain no instrument that would distinguish a real gain from none, and the deskilling result shows that such a world can be quietly negative. It ends when liability attaches to an outcome rather than to an equivalence.
positions.domains: All of them, symmetrically. That is the position's content: the classes are not separated at the horizon because no instrument separates them, and claims about which one landed are made by the party selling it.
positions.lag: Undefined by construction. A stock of this shape carries no measured flow, so the interval between a capability existing and a person being better off cannot be computed from it, only asserted — which is what most published intervals are.
positions.who: Unknown, and the not-knowing is not evenly distributed. Four of 86 trials in low- and middle-income countries means the populations with the least health system behind them are also the ones the record is quietest about, so the absence of evidence compounds in the same direction as every other gap on this axis.

edges.basis: Nine additional years of a running research loop before the horizon, standing against gates whose durations are set outside the laboratory — a 52-week endpoint, a payment code, a plant. Faster capability enlarges the throughput that stays inside.
More shots at the same funnel. 117 assets were in interventional trials in 2026 with 8 through Phase 2; a loop running from 2028 adds candidates, not trial years.
The class with no gate in front of it converts a capability date almost directly into a deployment date — under two years from published model to operations at an intergovernmental centre.
A research loop first running between 2037 and 2050 cannot put an originated molecule through discovery, a 52-week pivotal read-out and an uptake curve inside the window.
With the loop late, the realised record at the horizon is what was already in flight — 1,524 device authorisations by March 2026 and two randomised read-outs, none of which needed a research loop.

A long capability window with the present evidentiary standard unchanged accumulates authorisations rather than outcome data; 333 clearances in 2025 and 92 in one quarter of 2026 on predicate equivalence.
A method asymptote leaves the 2026 deployment stock as the whole story, and that stock is overwhelmingly image and signal reading inside rich health systems.
The candidate cohort stops refilling while the trial clock runs unchanged, so the eight assets past Phase 2 become the ceiling rather than the leading edge.
Throughput gains that compound off a still-improving frontier stop compounding at an asymptote.
Rungs inside one year compress the capability side and leave the trial, payment and construction clocks untouched, which widens the interval between what exists and what arrives.
Deployment outruns evidence production fastest when capability steps are close together, and under a far slower cadence only 76 of 1,978 registered studies had posted results by August 2026.
A short rung interval does not shorten a 52-week endpoint or a 47-centre enrolment.
A gap past five years gives the institutional side time to build a payment route and a programme around tools that already exist.
A long interval between rungs gives throughput time to leave the building.

The same failure mode in a second instrument. Measurement unanchored on control is the world in which nobody built the apparatus that would say whether an outcome moved either, and 1,466 of 1,524 authorisations cleared on equivalence rather than on an outcome.
Near-misses recurring is the deployed-and-harmful direction, and the one measured instance has exactly that shape: unassisted adenoma detection down 6.0 points after the tools arrived.
Recurring near-misses force evidence into existence, which is the thing a record that cannot say is missing.

A field-wide tractable result is the condition under which a regulator accepts a model-based endpoint; a pathology tool was qualified for any sponsor in December 2025 and an in-silico liver model accepted in June 2026.
The same qualification machinery is an evidence instrument, and qualification is how one company's validated tool becomes checkable infrastructure.
Control lost undetected and a ledger running against the recipient are the same event seen at two scales — a system doing its stated job while the measured net moves the other way.
A catch that buys a pause is proof that someone was measuring, and the institutions that measured are the ones that would measure an outcome.
A halt leaves the already-authorised device and screening stock as the entire realised record at the horizon.
A halt reaches the discovery step. Assets already in Phase 2 survive it; the cohort behind them stops.
Throughput inside the laboratory is precisely what a halt is built to stop.
A verified limit requires standing international measurement machinery, and that is the same institutional stock running universal early-warning coverage toward its end-2027 target.
Unilateral controls withhold capability from exactly the countries this class serves — those holding under 0.1 percent of world data-centre capacity and under 1 percent of generative traffic.

An executive release gate is an institution that also grants priority review and qualifies development tools; a national priority voucher pilot targeting one to two months against a ten-to-twelve-month review had granted 15 by early 2026.
A national release gate is not a delivery channel in the countries this class reaches, and it adds a permission step to a class whose advantage is needing none.
A civil regime enforced forces outcome evidence into production, because liability attaches to the outcome rather than to the equivalence.
Same mechanism, positive direction: a regime paying for a demonstrated outcome creates the route that 1,524 authorisations currently meet with three permanent codes.
Developer commitments are self-declared benefit with no external instrument, which is this position's definition rather than a consequence of it.
A contested patchwork is what an organised national screening programme cannot be built on, and the programme is what made the one strong result possible.
Work not delivered to standard is the throughput-inside-the-laboratory world seen from the client's side of the counter.
Broad absorption is how a tool reaches an organised programme; the Swedish trial cut reading workload 44 percent, which is an absorption result and an outcome result in the same measurement.

Absorption raises the chance a gain is real and the chance nobody measures it. 71 percent of United States acute-care hospitals used integrated predictive tools in 2024 while the only systematic study of use called adoption nascent and concentrated.
A displacement shock is the direction in which the ledger runs against the person; the same assistant moved Kenyan high performers up 15 percent and low performers down 8.
Displacement at that scale implies capability deep enough to have reached the laboratory bench, which is where the candidate cohort is generated.
Power and siting binding is this position's mechanism seen from a household bill: 28.92 to 329.17 dollars per megawatt-day and about 70 dollars a month per household by 2028.
Concentrated capacity is captured throughput by construction — 0.7 percent of one fleet recovered continuously for over a year accrues to that fleet's owner and to nobody else.

Diversified capacity is the condition under which inference reaches the countries holding under 0.1 percent of world data-centre capacity and served 80 percent of their traffic from another continent.
Power binding raises the cost of the inference this class depends on being nearly free; its whole advantage is three to four orders of magnitude below the physics model.
Acquiescence through use is the world in which nobody demands the outcome evidence, and it is not produced because nobody bills for it.
Local opposition is largely about siting and the bill, which is this position's mechanism; 71 percent opposed a local data centre in March 2026 against 53 percent opposing a local nuclear plant.
A backlash coalition holding national office is how an outcome-evidence mandate gets written, and the mandate is what ends this position.
The same coalition slows procurement of tools whose benefit is asserted rather than demonstrated, and 96.2 percent of the stock was cleared on assertion of equivalence.
A 320-patient 52-week pivotal programme and the plant behind it are funded objects; a boom funds the cohort behind the first one.
The first thing a correction cuts is a trial with a 2029 read-out — one company cut or paused five programmes including three clinical ones in May 2025 under far milder stress.
Capital expenditure cuts reach the pivotal programmes and the fill-finish capacity before they reach the models.
A forecast whose compute cost per run fell three to four orders of magnitude survives a capital-expenditure cut intact, and becomes the largest surviving realised gain by default.
A displacement demand crisis is a measured welfare loss landing on the receiving side, which is this position's quantity.
A commercial cadence sells throughput, and throughput is the gain that does not leave the building.
Benefit asserted by the party selling it is the record that cannot say, and the 44-percent-more-materials estimate withdrawn in May 2025 is the worked example.
Frontier declined and scope confined leaves the deployment stock inside health systems as the realised record.
Confined scope is fully compatible with this class, whose operational model is small, cheap and already public along with its weights.
State-directed procurement is how a pivotal programme is funded and a regulator is moved; the flagship pivotal trial runs 47 centres inside a single state's health system.
Refusals held and rules sought is the conduct that produces qualified development tools other sponsors may use without revalidating them.
Laboratories seeking rules produce evidence other parties can check, which is the apparatus this position lacks.

againstCase:
Four arguments, and the first three are strong enough that I would not be surprised to lose on them.

ONE — THIS PROJECT'S OWN DEFECT IS A COUNTING DEFECT, AND THIS ADDS COUNTS. Five recorded instances now of a surface rendering a letter or a quantifier that inherited a meaning or a domain it was not written for. The current sheet already carries 24 of 49 positions unreachable by any rule, authored figures keyed to r4 letters drawing on an r6 page, 22 rows of which 13 are wrong, and a crisis card asserting no superintelligence off a band that now means arrival between 2037 and 2050. An eleventh axis is six more positions and fifty-seven more edges added to exactly the structure that keeps failing, and the failure mode is not carelessness but scale — the coverage declaration caught every authored string through two rebuilds in one night and never saw the 26 figures, because a declaration protects only what it declares. The counts gate exists and found four of five unaided, which is the reason to think this is survivable, not a reason to think it is free.

TWO — THE RULE LIBRARY CANNOT HEAR THIS AXIS, AND AN AXIS THAT NEVER MOVES IS WORSE THAN NO AXIS. All 26 rules carry a fixed nudge vector, two of them supply 52 percent of all 79 applications, and the matcher only ever sees the first 300 characters of an event with 81 percent of those cut mid-word. There is no rule whose subject is a clinical read-out, a payment code, a screening programme, a flood warning or an authorisation count. G would launch in exactly P's condition — one application ever, or none — and a position that never moves renders as a live reading when it is a frozen prior, which is the most dangerous object this document can contain, because it looks like a measurement. P is sitting in the file right now as the worked example, and the honest sequencing argument is that the rule library should be extended to take benefit as a subject first, and the axis added afterward when there is something for it to hear.

THREE — EVERY DEFENSIBLE EDGE RUNS INTO IT. I wrote fifty-seven edges and all of them are inbound. I tried to construct outbound edges and could not defend one: a world where flood warning reaches 460 million people does not change what two governments settle, what the laboratories choose, or when the research loop closes. An axis that only receives is a readout, and a readout belongs on the crisis board or in the claims register, where it can be checked against a witness, rather than in the position space, where it will absorb probability mass from the axes that actually drive the network and will make the ensemble look richer than it is. The counter is that P is also largely downstream and is an axis — but P at least drives R and C, and G drives nothing.

FOUR — THE INSTRUMENT IS A STOCK WITH NO MEASURED FLOW. The three sharpest numbers here — zero approvals, 1,524 authorisations, three permanent payment codes — are all current-state facts, and the only rate that is well measured, authorisations rising from 65 in 2018 to 333 in 2025, counts paperwork rather than benefit. Forecasting a 2036 state from a stock whose flow nobody has measured is the shape of the window-label defect, which this project has now made twice. The cheapest correct response to the reader may not be an axis at all: write the two clocks into the prose with the one drug that worked as the demonstration — discovery compressed to 12 to 18 months, pivotal read-out 30 October 2029 — and let the reference text's own author supply the concession, since he made it in July 2026. That is a paragraph, and this is a structural change bought to fix a paragraph.

WHAT SURVIVES ALL FOUR. The forecast currently has no way to say that a capability existed, was deployed, did paid work and cured nothing — it can only say that by accident, as the residue of ten axes none of which asked. The residue is already a coverage map showing 87 percent unexplained with six axes moving zero. Adding an axis nothing can move makes that map worse in the short run and honest in the long run, and the choice between those is a scheduling decision rather than a design one.

evidence.question: Weather forecasting: what has AI actually delivered, measured, and is it operational?
evidence.answer: This is the strongest realised case outside health, and the only one where a frontier-lab method sits inside a public operational service delivering a public good. ECMWF put its machine-learned AIFS Single into operations on 25 February 2025 and AIFS-ENS on 1 July 2025 — the first national/intergovernmental weather centre to run an ML model as a headline product. ECMWF's own 2025 verification (Newsletter 187, 2026) reports medium-range error reductions of 5-15% against the physics-based IFS, precipitation improved ~10% in the medium range, and AIFS v2 cutting significant-wave-height error ~10%. Crucially the gain is verified against radiosonde and SYNOP observations, not only against the analysis the model was initialised from — an independent check most industry claims lack. On tropical cyclones, Google DeepMind's WeatherNext Cyclones was co-developed with the US National Hurricane Center, CIRA and the UK Met Office and ran experimentally through the 2025 Atlantic season; NHC used it in the Hurricane Melissa rapid-intensification and Jamaica landfall forecast (October 2025). Weights and code are public. The receiving party here is a government forecaster and, through it, the public — not a paying enterprise customer. Compute cost per forecast fell by roughly three to four orders of magnitude versus NWP, which is what makes national adoption in poor countries conceivable.
evidence.figures: AIFS Single operational 25 Feb 2025; AIFS-ENS operational 1 Jul 2025 (ECMWF). Medium-range error reduction 5-15% vs IFS; precipitation +~10% skill in medium range; AIFS v2 wave-height error -10%, 4-6% improvement upper-air and near-surface (ECMWF Newsletter 185/187, 2025-2026). WeatherNext Cyclones 5-day track error 230 km vs 370 km for the ECMWF ensemble; ~3.75 kt better than HAFS on 3-day intensity; ~1 day extra lead time on track, intensity and wind radii (Google DeepMind, 2025-2026).
evidence.uncertainty: The skill gain is well established and independently verified. What is NOT established is the outcome gain: no published study yet converts the extra ~24 hours of cyclone lead time into evacuated populations, avoided deaths or avoided property loss. Warning lead time is a necessary but not sufficient condition — the 2025-26 US National Weather Service staffing reductions are a live example of the last-mile capacity that converts a forecast into a protected person degrading while the forecast improves.

evidence.question: Weather forecasting: where do the AI models fail, and does the failure matter?
evidence.answer: The failure is precisely at the events that justify the forecast. A May 2026 Science Advances study led by Karlsruhe Institute of Technology and the University of Geneva compared GraphCast, Pangu-Weather and FuXi against the physics-based HRES and found the AI models consistently worse on record-breaking events, systematically underestimating both the intensity and the frequency of extremes, with the underestimation growing the further the event exceeds anything in the 1979-2017 training window. The mechanism is structural, not a bug: models trained to minimise mean error regress novel extremes toward the historical mean, and physics-based models are not so constrained because they solve equations rather than recall precedent. ECMWF's own verification independently notes AIFS has a larger tropical-cyclone intensity bias than IFS even while beating it on track. This is a general and transferable lesson for the axis: an AI system's realised benefit is largest in the regime it has seen most and smallest in the regime that matters most, and climate change moves the distribution the wrong way.
evidence.figures: Science Advances, published May 2026 (KIT/UNIGE-led). Training data span 1979-2017. AI models show 'consistently larger forecast errors for record-breaking events'; underestimation of heat, cold and wind records scales with record exceedance. ECMWF 2025 verification: AIFS beats IFS on TC track, worse on TC intensity bias.
evidence.uncertainty: The study tested models trained through 2017 and ending before AIFS v2 and WeatherNext; newer models with longer training windows and CRPS-style probabilistic losses may narrow the gap, and vendors dispute the generality. But the extrapolation problem is architectural, so partial improvement rather than resolution is the reasonable expectation. Contested range: AI-vs-physics on extremes is currently the single most active dispute in operational meteorology.

evidence.question: Does any AI system deliver a measured benefit to people outside rich countries and outside the industry?
evidence.answer: Flood forecasting is the clearest instance in the whole survey. Google Research published global extreme-flood prediction for ungauged watersheds in Nature (March 2024), showing reliability at up to five days lead time in basins with no gauges — matching or beating the Copernicus GloFAS nowcast, i.e. AI delivered five days of warning where the incumbent system delivered essentially zero. Flood Hub now covers river basins in more than 150 countries, roughly 1,800 sites and a population of about 460 million, and the model, framework and training approach were open-sourced in June 2026 so national hydrological services can train their own. WMO is piloting AI flood forecasting in Nigeria, Viet Nam, Uruguay, Malawi and the Czech Republic under Early Warnings for All (target: universal coverage by end-2027). This is the domain where the recipient is unambiguously not the industry: ungauged basins are, almost by definition, poor places. It is also the domain with the shortest lag from capability to a person being better off — because no factory, clinic, regulator or capital stock sits in between. The gating factor is a mobile phone and a local warning channel, not a trial or a permit.
evidence.figures: Nature, March 2024: reliable extreme-flood prediction to 5-day lead time in ungauged basins, equal to or better than GloFAS nowcast (0-day). Flood Hub: 150+ countries, ~1,800 sites, ~460M people covered (2026). 2026 model upgrade: +6 days reliable horizon in gauged basins, +1 day in ungauged. Framework open-sourced June 2026. WMO Early Warnings for All target: end-2027.
evidence.uncertainty: Coverage is not the same as receipt. There is no published estimate of how many of the 460M people covered actually received and acted on a warning, and a 2026 responsible-modelling critique in Environmental Modelling questions whether the system was deployment-ready at the point it was declared so. Lives saved: unquantified. The gap between 'a forecast exists for your river' and 'you moved' is the whole unmeasured middle.

evidence.question: Materials and chemistry: did the headline AI discoveries produce real materials?
evidence.answer: No, not yet, and the record here is the sharpest correction of a capability claim in the survey. DeepMind's GNoME (Nature, November 2023) announced 2.2 million predicted crystals and 380,000 stable candidates, described as equivalent to '800 years of knowledge'. Cheetham and Seshadri's analysis (Chemistry of Materials, April 2024) examined the listings and concluded they had 'yet to find any strikingly novel compounds', characterising most as trivial dopant variants, symmetry-broken duplicates or chemically implausible high-element-count compositions. The companion Berkeley A-Lab paper (Nature, November 2023), which claimed 41 novel inorganic compounds autonomously synthesised in 17 days, drew a critique led by Robert Palgrave (UCL) arguing the compounds were largely already in the Inorganic Crystal Structure Database or misidentified; Nature issued a correction to the A-Lab paper in January 2026 — a two-year lag between claim and correction. A June 2026 preprint analysing 167,500 ICSD structures found that 0.0% of GNoME, 4.9% of MatterGen and 1.9% of Alexandria proposals share compositions with the post-1980 experimentally realised set, and that computed proposals in general — not just generative-AI ones — depart from the structural patterns real synthesis follows. The single clearest counterexample is Microsoft/PNNL's sodium-lithium solid electrolyte (January 2024): 32 million candidates screened computationally, a working solid-state battery built and tested, under nine months end to end. As of mid-2026 there is no commercial product from it. That is the shape of the whole domain: prediction is fast, synthesis is slow, and qualification into a product is slower still.
evidence.figures: GNoME: 2.2M structures, 380k stable, Nature Nov 2023. Cheetham & Seshadri critique April 2024. A-Lab: 41 compounds in 17 days claimed Nov 2023; Nature correction issued January 2026. arXiv 2606.30967 (June 2026): 0.0% / 4.9% / 1.9% composition overlap with post-1980 ICSD for GNoME / MatterGen / Alexandria; 82.9% of new experimental formulas enter pre-existing structural communities; new-community formation fell from 40.2% (1930s) to 2.6% (2010s). Microsoft/PNNL: 32M candidates screened, <9 months to working prototype (Jan 2024); zero commercial products as of Aug 2026.
evidence.uncertainty: Contested. DeepMind maintains GNoME expanded the stable-materials space and that novelty should be judged on structure space rather than named compounds; the June 2026 preprint is not yet peer-reviewed and its own finding is that ALL computed sets, including the physics-based Materials Project, depart from experimental basins — which weakens the specifically anti-AI reading. What is not contested is that no AI-proposed inorganic material had entered commercial production as of mid-2026. The honest range on 'time from AI proposal to a material in a shipped product' is 5-15 years and nobody has yet completed one lap.

evidence.question: Was there fabricated evidence in the AI-for-science literature, and what did it distort?
evidence.answer: Yes, and it was the single most-cited quantitative estimate of AI's effect on materials research. Aidan Toner-Rodgers' paper 'Artificial Intelligence, Scientific Discovery, and Product Innovation' (preprint December 2024) claimed that materials scientists given an AI discovery tool found 44% more materials, filed 39% more patents and produced 17% more downstream product innovation. It was covered by the Wall Street Journal, Nature and The Atlantic and endorsed by David Autor and Daron Acemoglu. In May 2025 MIT stated it had no confidence in the provenance, reliability or validity of the data or the veracity of the research, asked that it be withdrawn from public discourse, and had it removed from arXiv; the author left MIT. Materials scientists had flagged the results as implausible. The paper was still being cited by a European research commissioner after the retraction. The implication for the axis is direct: the best-known point estimate for AI's productivity effect on a physical science was fiction, and the field's residual evidence base is correspondingly thinner than the discourse suggests.
evidence.figures: Claimed: +44% materials discovered, +39% patent filings, +17% product innovation (preprint Dec 2024). MIT disavowal and arXiv withdrawal: May 2025. Approximately 1,000 materials scientists in the claimed sample; the firm was never identified.
evidence.uncertainty: No formal finding of fabrication has been published by a journal; MIT's statement is a disavowal, not an adjudicated misconduct finding. Nothing turns on the distinction for our purposes: the number should not be used.

evidence.question: Energy and the grid: what is measured, what is promised, and who pays?
evidence.answer: Almost all realised grid gains come from narrow forecasting and sensing ML, not frontier models, and they are real but modest. UK National Grid's dynamic line rating programme — ambient/weather forecasting feeding thermal ratings — increased line capacity 31% on average on its first project, freeing about a gigawatt and saving customers about £14m a year; in April 2026 it contracted 585 km more with potential savings up to about $66m/yr. PJM implemented advanced ambient ratings in March 2026, with MISO and NYISO not expected until 2028. Most US investor-owned utilities now run production ML for demand forecasting and asset health. The frontier-lab contribution is prospective: Google's Tapestry and PJM announced an AI partnership in 2025 to speed the interconnection queue — a queue holding roughly 79 GW solar, 37 GW storage, 23 GW wind and 4 GW gas with a two-year study cycle — with phased rollout beginning 2026 and no published throughput result yet. Against this, the industry's own demand has made electricity more expensive for everyone else: PJM capacity prices went from $28.92/MW-day (2024/25) to $329.17/MW-day (2026/27, at the FERC cap), with data centres identified as the majority driver of the increase, roughly $9.3bn of added capacity cost in one auction and about $70/month per household projected by 2028 across PJM territory. Six states have introduced construction moratoriums and seven have moved against data-centre tax incentives. This is the cleanest available instance of a domain where the capability's realised effect on the non-industry public, to date, is net negative.
evidence.figures: National Grid DLR: +31% average line capacity, ~£14m/yr (~$19m) consumer saving on first project; April 2026 contract for 585 km, up to ~$66m/yr potential. PJM advanced ambient rating live March 2026. PJM capacity price $28.92/MW-day (2024/25) → $329.17/MW-day (2026/27 cap); data centres ~63% of one auction's increase, +$9.3bn; ~$70/month per PJM household by 2028 (NRDC/IEEFA estimates); $100-163bn cumulative through 2033 absent intervention (NRDC). PJM queue as of Jan 2025: 79 GW solar, 37 GW storage, 23 GW wind, 4 GW gas; ~2-year study time.
evidence.uncertainty: The attribution of PJM price rises to data centres specifically is contested — SemiAnalysis and others argue generator retirements, gas-turbine supply constraints and delayed transmission explain much of it, and that capacity cost is a modest share of a retail bill. The range on 'data-centre share of the increase' runs roughly 40-70% depending on method. Vendor claims of 25-40% reductions in unplanned outages from predictive maintenance are unaudited and should not be relied on. Utility ML savings are real but nearly all pre-date the frontier-model era.

evidence.question: Fusion and fission: has AI delivered energy?
evidence.answer: No energy, some genuine control and paperwork gains. DeepMind and EPFL's Swiss Plasma Centre demonstrated deep-RL magnetic control of tokamak plasma on the live TCV device (Nature, February 2022), with a policy trained wholly in simulation shaping and holding plasma configurations conventional controllers struggle with. In October 2025 DeepMind and Commonwealth Fusion Systems announced a partnership applying TORAX simulation plus RL/AlphaEvolve-style search to SPARC operating scenarios; Google has worked with TAE Technologies for roughly a decade. None of this has produced net electricity, and SPARC's own Q>1 milestone is a 2027-ish target independent of AI. On fission the measured result is administrative rather than physical: DOE, Idaho National Laboratory, Argonne, Microsoft and Everstar demonstrated in 2026 the AI-assisted generation of a 208-page reactor licensing document in one day against a stated typical four-to-six-week team effort, under the INL-led Prometheus programme; INL and NVIDIA state a goal of halving reactor development time and operating cost. This is a useful illustration for the axis: where the bottleneck is document production and regulatory translation, AI compresses it immediately and measurably; where the bottleneck is a physical plant or a plasma, it does not.
evidence.figures: DeepMind/EPFL TCV RL plasma control: Nature, 16 Feb 2022. DeepMind-CFS partnership announced 16 Oct 2025. Prometheus/INL demonstration (2026): 208-page licensing document generated in 1 day vs typical 4-6 weeks. INL-NVIDIA stated goal: 50% cut in reactor development time and operating cost. Net fusion electricity delivered to any grid attributable to AI as of Aug 2026: zero.
evidence.uncertainty: The licensing figure is a single demonstration reported by the participants, not an audited before/after across a licensing docket, and the NRC has not accepted an AI-generated application on a shortened schedule. Whether faster document production shortens the binding constraint — NRC review capacity and public process — is unproven and plausibly false. Fusion timelines remain contested by decades.

evidence.question: Agriculture: what has AI measurably changed on farms, and for whom?
evidence.answer: One sharp success surrounded by a broad null. John Deere's See & Spray — camera-plus-CNN targeted herbicide application — covered more than 5 million acres in the 2025 US season and, on Deere's figures, saved about 31 million gallons of herbicide mix, with average herbicide savings of 59% across corn, soybean and cotton; an Iowa State University study reported 76% average product savings and $15.7/acre economic savings. Deere prices it at $1/fallow acre or $5/in-crop acre under a savings guarantee, which is itself evidence the gain is real enough to underwrite. The beneficiaries beyond the farm are plausible — less herbicide in watersheds — but no measured environmental outcome has been published. Against this, the broader precision-agriculture record is a null: a March 2026 Purdue analysis of 570 Kansas farms over 2002-2022 (Kansas Farm Management Association data, DEA methodology) found that of 17 technology bundles only two — automated guidance alone, and yield monitors with grid soil sampling — showed statistically meaningful efficiency gains, and that the added costs of most bundles are not on average overcome by the revenue gains. Adoption is nonetheless high (automated guidance ~80%, yield monitors >60%, variable-rate seed 15% by 2022), and concentrated in large farms. For smallholders, generative-AI advisory tools (Farmer.Chat, deployed in Kenya, India, Ethiopia and Nigeria) are running a cluster-RCT across 600 villages in Nakuru County, Kenya, under J-PAL — and the results are not out. As of mid-2026 there is no causal evidence that an AI advisory tool raises a smallholder's yield or income.
evidence.figures: See & Spray: >5M acres in 2025 season; ~31M gallons herbicide mix saved (Deere, Nov 2025); 59% average herbicide savings corn/soy/cotton (Deere); 76% product savings and $15.7/acre (Iowa State study); pricing $1/fallow acre, $5/in-crop acre. Purdue/KFMA March 2026: 570 farms, 2002-2022, 2 of 17 bundles with meaningful efficiency gains. 2022 adoption: auto-guidance ~80%, yield monitors >60%, section control ~50%, grid soil sampling 40%, variable-rate fertiliser >20%, variable-rate seed 15%. Farmer.Chat RCT: 600 villages, Nakuru County Kenya, results pending as of Aug 2026.
evidence.uncertainty: The See & Spray figures are vendor-reported except the Iowa State study; the 59% and 76% numbers are not directly comparable (different fields, crops, weed pressures) and the true range across conditions is probably 30-80%. Whether herbicide reduction reaches consumers as lower food prices or cleaner water is entirely unmeasured. The Purdue null covers 2002-2022 and therefore mostly pre-AI precision agriculture; it does not falsify See & Spray, but it is the best available base rate for how often a farm-technology gain survives contact with costs.

evidence.question: Logistics and freight: what is the measured gain?
evidence.answer: The weakest evidence base in the survey relative to the volume of claims. Driverless freight is real but tiny: Aurora had logged over 250,000 driverless miles across ten commercial lanes by early 2026 with no driver-attributed collisions, including a ~1,000-mile Fort Worth-Phoenix lane exceeding federal hours-of-service limits for a human; it guides 2026 revenue of $14-16m and targets ~200 driverless trucks and an $80m run-rate exiting 2026. Kodiak logged over 10,700 hours of paid driverless operation by end-2025. Against roughly 3.5 million US truck drivers and a multi-trillion-dollar freight market, this is a rounding error, and the freight market's actual 2023-2026 price movements are explained by an overcapacity recession, not by automation. Warehouse and route-optimisation claims — '$4bn annual savings', '73% transfer efficiency', '100 million miles eliminated' — trace to vendor and trade-press material with no auditable methodology, and I could not find an independent study establishing a logistics-wide productivity gain attributable to AI. Ship weather-routing claims cluster at 5-15% fuel savings per voyage, again vendor-reported; the IMO's 8% maritime CO2 reduction is not attributable to AI specifically. The one genuinely instructive negative from adjacent history: automated container terminals have repeatedly underperformed manual ones on move-per-hour productivity, which is the standing warning against reading capital deployment as realised gain.
evidence.figures: Aurora: >250,000 driverless miles, 10 commercial lanes, zero driver-attributed collisions (early 2026); 2026 revenue guidance $14-16m; target >200 driverless trucks and ~$80m run-rate exiting 2026. Kodiak: >10,700 hours paid driverless operations by end-2025, +106% QoQ. Vendor claims (unaudited): $4bn/yr warehouse robotics savings; 73% transfer-efficiency gain at one Beijing facility; 5-15% ship fuel savings; DSV $50m AMR rollout; Walmart $1bn automation.
evidence.uncertainty: High. Almost every logistics figure in circulation is self-reported by a party selling the technology. Treat the 5-15% routing and 10-20% warehouse figures as an upper bound on best cases, not a sector average. No freight-rate, delivery-time or shelf-price series shows an identifiable AI break as of mid-2026. The autonomous-trucking safety record is real but the exposure (250k miles) is far too small to establish a safety rate against the human baseline of roughly one fatal crash per 100 million truck miles.

evidence.question: Mathematics: is AI producing new results, and does that count as a realised gain?
evidence.answer: Yes to the first, and it is the fastest-moving domain in the survey — because verification is cheap and the physical world is absent. Between August 2025 and August 2026 the Erdős problems database went from a small trickle to 565 of 1,217 problems solved, with AI implicated in a substantial and growing share. Dated milestones: 6 January 2026, Harmonic's Aristotle produced a formal Lean proof of Problem #728; January 2026, a DeepMind team solved 4 problems and rediscovered solutions to 9; May 2026, a separate DeepMind team autonomously resolved 9 of 353 open problems at a few hundred dollars per problem; 20 May 2026, an OpenAI internal model disproved the Erdős planar unit-distance conjecture, open roughly 80 years — Tim Gowers said he would have recommended acceptance to the Annals without hesitation; 1 August 2026, OpenAI's Astra reported 10 further advances. Notably, many results came from hobbyists and undergraduates using publicly available models, not from lab staff. On the infrastructure side AlphaEvolve (May 2025) found a 4x4 complex matrix multiplication using 48 scalar multiplications against Strassen's 49 — a 56-year record — recovered state of the art on ~75% of 50+ open problems and improved it on ~20%, and its scheduling heuristic has recovered roughly 0.7% of Google's worldwide compute continuously for over a year, equivalent to about 14,000 servers. That last figure is the single most credible hard-dollar realised gain in this entire survey, and it accrues to the company that built the model.
evidence.figures: Erdős database: 565 solved / 652 open of 1,217 as of Aug 2026 (Bloom). Aristotle formal Lean proof of #728, 6 Jan 2026. DeepMind Jan 2026: 4 solved, 9 rediscovered. DeepMind May 2026: 9 of 353 open problems autonomously, few hundred USD each. OpenAI unit-distance conjecture disproof, 20 May 2026 (~80 years open). OpenAI Astra, 1 Aug 2026: 10 further advances. AlphaEvolve (May 2025): 4x4 complex matmul in 48 multiplications vs Strassen's 49 (record standing since 1969); SOTA matched on ~75% and improved on ~20% of 50+ problems; ~0.7% of Google fleet compute recovered continuously for >1 year, ≈14,000 servers, estimated $42-70m/yr.
evidence.uncertainty: Two live problems. First, verification: Thomas Bloom notes that many AI-produced proofs run 100-200 pages and no human has read them, so the solved count partly outruns the checked count — formalisation in Lean is the mitigation and is not universal. Second, significance: the resolved problems range from obscure (#728) to genuinely major (unit distance), and Noga Alon has stopped working on such problems, which is an ambiguous signal. The gain to anyone outside mathematics is, so far, entirely indirect. The $42-70m AlphaEvolve estimate is a third-party inference, not a Google disclosure; the 0.7% is Google's own.

evidence.question: Software as an input to every other field: does AI-assisted coding actually deliver?
evidence.answer: The most rigorous evidence says no, or not yet, for experienced developers on real code. METR's randomised trial (tasks run Feb-June 2025, published 10 July 2025) found 16 experienced open-source maintainers took 19% LONGER on 246 real tasks in their own repositories when allowed AI tools, while believing they had been 20% faster — a 39-point perception gap. METR's 24 February 2026 update reports a late-2025 rerun: -18% (CI -38% to +9%) for returning developers and -4% (CI -15% to +9%) for newly recruited ones, and METR is abandoning the design because 30-50% of developers refused to submit tasks they did not want to do without AI, biasing the sample toward tasks where AI helps least. So the honest reading is: the slowdown finding has not been overturned, but the newer estimates are too selection-contaminated to carry weight in either direction. Meanwhile DORA's 2025 report puts AI adoption among software professionals at 90% (up 14 points) and estimates throughput improved 2-18% — a reversal from 2024, when every 25% rise in adoption was associated with a ~1.5% throughput drop — while the negative relationship with delivery stability persisted through both years. The pattern that survives: AI raises change volume, and organisations without strong testing and fast feedback convert that volume into instability. Absolute adoption in the wider economy remains low: US Census BTOS puts AI use among all businesses at 17-20% from December 2025 to May 2026 (19.8% national), 39.7% in Information and 33.9% in Finance, but ~14% in retail, and 37% among firms of 250+ employees against a much lower small-firm rate.
evidence.figures: METR July 2025: -19% speedup, i.e. 19% slower (CI: +2% to +39% longer), 16 developers, 246 tasks, Feb-Jun 2025; developers predicted +24% and estimated +20% after the fact. METR Feb 2026 update: returning devs -18% (CI -38% to +9%), new recruits -4% (CI -15% to +9%); 30-50% of developers withheld tasks. DORA 2025: 90% adoption (+14pp); throughput +2-18%; stability still negatively associated. DORA 2024: each +25% adoption ≈ -1.5% throughput, -7.2% stability. US Census BTOS: 17-20% of businesses using AI, Dec 2025-May 2026; 19.8% national, 39.7% Information, 33.9% Finance, ~14% Retail; 37% of firms with 250+ employees.
evidence.uncertainty: METR's sample is small, expert, and drawn from mature repositories where the developer has deep context — the condition least favourable to AI and least representative of most coding. DORA is correlational and self-reported. The two disagree, and the disagreement is genuine and unresolved as of mid-2026: nobody has a clean causal estimate of AI's effect on software output at scale. Range of defensible estimates for experienced-developer speedup: -20% to +20%.

evidence.question: At the macro level, is any of this showing up as realised output?
evidence.answer: The money is overwhelmingly flowing INTO AI, not out of it. US real GDP grew about 2.1% annualised in Q1 2026, with AI-related investment — data-centre equipment, structures and software — accounting for roughly three-quarters of that growth; AI data-centre, hardware and networking investment reached about 1.4% of GDP in Q1 2026, doubled from ~0.7%, the highest capital-formation reading of its kind since the late-1990s telecom cycle. Bridgewater puts the AI capex boost to US growth at ~140bp in 2026 and ~150bp in 2027. That is input spending: it registers as growth because it is purchased, not because it made anything cheaper. On the output side, measured productivity is good but not anomalous — nonfarm business labour productivity averaged 2.2%/yr over 2019Q4-2025Q4 (the second-best cycle since 1973, behind the dotcom era) and sits ~2.2% above CBO's pre-pandemic forecast — and the econometric attribution to AI is weak: one review puts a 10% rise in AI investment at a 0.02pp increase in reported labour productivity growth. MIT's NANDA study (August 2025) found 95% of enterprise generative-AI pilots produced no measurable P&L impact, based on 150 interviews, 350 employee surveys and 300 public deployments — a finding widely over-read, since 'no measurable P&L impact' is not 'the pilot failed', but its direction is not in dispute. The one large realised gain that IS measured accrues to consumers rather than firms: Brynjolfsson, Collis, Eggers, Kazinnik and Nguyen (April 2026) estimate US aggregate consumer surplus from generative AI rose from $116bn (July 2025) to $172bn (March 2026), far exceeding US generative-AI revenue. But the distribution matters more than the total: mean willingness-to-accept was $124.50/month while the MEDIAN was $11.40. Half of users would give it up for the price of a sandwich.
evidence.figures: Q1 2026: US real GDP +2.1% annualised, AI-related investment ~75% of growth; AI datacentre/hardware/networking = 1.4% of GDP, up from 0.7%. Bridgewater: ~140bp growth boost 2026, ~150bp 2027. BLS/Furman: 2.2%/yr productivity 2019Q4-2025Q4; 2.8% 1-yr, 2.5% 2-yr; 2.2% above CBO pre-pandemic path. Elasticity estimate: +10% AI investment ≈ +0.02pp labour productivity growth. MIT NANDA (Aug 2025): 95% of GenAI pilots with no measurable P&L impact; n=150 interviews, 350 surveys, 300 deployments. Brynjolfsson et al. (April 2026): mean WTA $98 (Jul 2025) → $124.50 (Mar 2026); median $3.40 → $11.40; adult users 98M → 115M; aggregate consumer surplus $116bn → $172bn.
evidence.uncertainty: The '75% of GDP growth' figure is arithmetically sensitive to how AI investment is bounded and to a single quarter; estimates in circulation range from ~40% to ~75% depending on definition. Consumer-surplus estimates from stated willingness-to-accept are known to overstate — hypothetical bias in WTA elicitation typically runs 1.5-3x. The productivity acceleration has plausible non-AI explanations (post-pandemic reallocation, labour-market churn, capital deepening) and the observation window is too short to separate them. Nobody has a defensible attribution of measured productivity growth to AI as of mid-2026.

evidence.question: What does Machines of Loving Grace actually claim, and what does it concede?
evidence.answer: Amodei's October 2024 essay claims a 'compressed 21st century' — 50 to 100 years of biological progress in 5 to 10 — across five areas: biology and physical health; neuroscience and mental health; economic development and poverty; peace and governance; work and meaning. Read carefully, the essay is far more hedged outside health than its reception suggests, and it names its own bottlenecks explicitly: the speed of the physical world ('cells and animals run at a fixed speed so experiments on them take a certain amount of time which may be irreducible'); data scarcity, where 'in its absence more intelligence does not help'; intrinsic complexity, where chaotic systems stay only marginally predictable regardless of intelligence; human constraints — law, clinical-trial bureaucracy, regulatory requirements, public willingness to adopt; and physical limits. His confidence is explicitly graded: highest for biology and neuroscience; medium for poverty and development, which he says face human constraints and intrinsic complexity; lowest for governance and work, which he calls fuzzier and offers no timeline for. His 20%/yr GDP growth figure for developing nations is labelled 'a dream scenario, not what happens by default'. For an axis about realised gains, the essay is best used as its own bottleneck taxonomy rather than as a base rate — the five constraints it names are, empirically, exactly the ones that separated the domains in this survey: weather and flood forecasting (no physical bottleneck, data-rich, short lag) delivered; materials and energy (physical world, capital stock, regulator) did not.
evidence.figures: Published October 2024. Core claim: 50-100 years of biological progress compressed into 5-10 years post-'powerful AI'. Five named areas. Five named bottlenecks: physical-world speed, data scarcity, intrinsic complexity, human constraints (law/trials/regulation/adoption), physical limits. Economic development: 20% annual GDP growth in developing nations as an explicit 'dream scenario, not what happens by default'. No timelines given for governance or for work and meaning.
evidence.uncertainty: The essay is an argument by a lab CEO with an obvious interest in the conclusion, and is explicitly framed as a best-case sketch conditional on powerful AI arriving. Other forecasters dispute the compression claim mainly on trial and regulatory grounds — the constraint Amodei himself lists but treats as tractable. Note the asymmetry that matters for the axis: the essay's confidence is HIGHEST for the domain (health) that is most trial- and regulation-bound, and lower for the domains where the physical bottlenecks are actually weakest.

evidence.question: Synthesis: what orders the domains, and how long is the lag from capability to a person being better off?
evidence.answer: The survey sorts cleanly on one variable — how much physical world, capital stock and institutional permission sits between the model output and the person. Four tiers emerge. TIER 1, lag under two years, gain realised and reaching non-industry people: forecasting where the output IS the product — weather (operational at ECMWF from Feb 2025), tropical cyclones (NHC, 2025 season), riverine floods (150+ countries, ~460M people). Nothing needs to be built; a forecast is consumed the moment it is issued. TIER 2, lag two to five years, gain realised but captured mostly by the producer: computation and mathematics — AlphaEvolve's 0.7% fleet compute recovery, Erdős-problem resolutions, refinery and grid control ML. Cheap verification, no physical construction, and the beneficiary is whoever owns the compute. TIER 3, lag five to fifteen years, gain not yet realised: materials, chemistry, batteries, fusion, autonomous freight — proposals and prototypes exist in volume, but synthesis, qualification, plant construction and fleet replacement each impose their own irreducible clock. The Microsoft/PNNL electrolyte went from 32 million candidates to a working cell in nine months and to a commercial product in zero years since. TIER 4, negative or null to date: broad precision agriculture (2 of 17 bundles profitable, Purdue 2026), enterprise generative-AI pilots (95% with no measurable P&L, MIT 2025), experienced-developer coding (METR, 2025-26), and grid ratepayers, who are paying more because of the industry's own demand. Three cross-cutting gates decide everything: whether verification is cheap (maths and code beat chemistry and biology by orders of magnitude); whether a physical clock intervenes (synthesis, growth, construction, fleet turnover); and whether an institution must consent (regulator, procurement, farmer, developer). And one distributional finding runs through all of it: the domains that reached non-industry people fastest — flood and cyclone warnings — did so precisely because they were given away rather than sold, while the domains with the largest audited dollar gains kept them inside the firm that built the model.
evidence.figures: Realised-lag estimates from this survey: forecasting <2 yr (ECMWF Feb 2025 to public benefit immediate); compute/maths 2-5 yr (AlphaEvolve May 2025, in production >1 yr, 0.7% of fleet); materials 5-15 yr and zero laps completed (GNoME Nov 2023 → commercial products as of Aug 2026: none); autonomous freight >10 yr at current scaling (250k driverless miles vs ~3.5M US truck drivers). Null tier: 2/17 precision-ag bundles profitable (Purdue, Mar 2026); 95% of enterprise pilots without measurable P&L (MIT, Aug 2025); -18% to -4% developer speedup (METR, Feb 2026). Distributional: median US user WTA $11.40/month vs mean $124.50 (Stanford, Apr 2026).
evidence.uncertainty: The tiering is my synthesis, not a published taxonomy, and the lag figures for tiers 3 and 4 are lower bounds — no AI-originated material or reactor has completed a full cycle to a shipped product, so the true lag is unobserved and could be far longer than 15 years or could collapse if AI compresses the qualification and regulatory steps as the INL licensing demonstration hints. The largest single unknown for the axis: whether the physical-world clock is genuinely irreducible (Amodei's own first bottleneck) or whether massively parallel automated experimentation eventually cuts it. As of mid-2026 there is no evidence either way, because no self-driving lab has yet produced a compound that reached market.

evidence.question: What exactly is the "compressed 21st century" thesis, and what are its time bounds?
evidence.answer:
Amodei's core prediction, verbatim: "my basic prediction is that AI-enabled biology and medicine will allow us to compress the progress that human biologists would have achieved over the next 50-100 years into 5-10 years. I'll refer to this as the 'compressed 21st century': the idea that after powerful AI is developed, we will in a few years make all the progress in biology and medicine that we would have made in the whole 21st century."

The mechanism is explicitly a rate multiplier on tool-discoveries, not on data analysis: "a surprisingly large fraction of the progress in biology has come from a truly tiny number of discoveries... There's perhaps ~1 of these major discoveries per year and collectively they arguably drive >50% of progress in biology." And: "I think their rate of discovery could be increased by 10x or more if there were a lot more talented, creative researchers... it's my guess that powerful AI could at least 10x the rate of these discoveries, giving us the next 50-100 years of biological progress in 5-10 years."

He rules out the faster version himself: "Why not 100x? Perhaps it is possible, but here both serial dependence and experiment times become important: getting 100 years of progress in 1 year requires a lot of things to go right the first time... I'm actually open to the (perhaps absurd-sounding) idea that we could get 1000 years of progress in 5-10 years, but very skeptical that we can get 100 years in 1 year."

CRITICAL FOR THE AXIS — the clock does not start at publication. The 5–10 years run AFTER "powerful AI" arrives: "it's helpful to specify clearly what we mean by powerful AI (i.e. the threshold at which the 5-10 year clock starts counting)". In Oct 2024 he wrote "I think it could come as early as 2026, though there are also ways it could take much longer." The essay states its own calendar date for the health outcomes exactly once, and it lands on the reader's headline year: "It is worth looking at this list and reflecting on how different the world will be if all of it is achieved 7-12 years from now (which would be in line with an aggressive AI timeline)." Written October 2024, that is 2031–2036. So the essay's own aggressive case has the full disease list arriving no earlier than 2031 and as late as 2036 — the year of the reader's headline — and that is conditional on powerful AI in 2026, which did not happen on that schedule (see Amodei's own Jan 2026 restatement, separate finding).
